source.title: Doubling constructions: Global functoriality for non-generic cuspidal representations
source.authors: Yuanqing Cai, Solomon Friedberg and Eyal Kaplan
source.version: arXiv v5, 20 May 2024, 60 pages, the version to be published in the Annals (arXiv comment); the Annals site gives pp. 893–966 but its PDF was not fetched. Numbering from v5; Unpaywall lists only v5 (also mirrored by Hokkaido University).
readSections: Review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): arXiv v5 (the same PDF, SHA-256 dd49d944…) and its TeX source read in full again, every item checked against it. The published version is paywalled and was not available to the review either.

summary: Cai, Friedberg and Kaplan prove that every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a split symplectic, special orthogonal or general spin group over a number field has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), without genericity and independently of the trace formula. They apply the converse theorem, controlling the twisted L-functions with the generalized doubling method: local poles in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 are attained by the doubling integrals through Kaplan's GL_c × GL_k integrals (Theorem 3.12, Appendix A), the doubling Eisenstein series is holomorphic away from twisted self-duality (Theorem 4.1), and so the twisted L-functions are entire (Theorem 4.8). They deduce that weak transfers are coarse transfers at every place and that local coarse transfers exist. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and one finding is recorded (a unitarity hypothesis in §3.6, repaired by a twist). Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24), of the 76 items 4 are planned and 72 are missing, all routed to the Part II; 18 source issues are recorded, the substantive ones being E1 and a swapped argument in the proof of Lemma 4.3.

items.name: The split groups G_l and the embedding r_G
items.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0. G_l is one of Sp_l (l even), SO_l or GSpin_l, split over F. For Sp_l and SO_l, G_l = {g ∈ SL_l : ᵗg J g = J}, with J_{Sp_l} = J_l diag(−I_{l/2}, I_{l/2}) and J_{SO_l} = J_l (J_l the antidiagonal permutation matrix). T and B are the diagonal and upper-triangular elements, and Sp_0, SO_0 and SO_1 are trivial. For GSpin_l with l > 2, put n = ⌊l/2⌋, X = ⊕_{i=0}^n Z e_i and X^∨ = ⊕_{i=0}^n Z e_i^∨ with the standard pairing. GSpin_l is the unique F-split group with based root datum (X, Δ, X^∨, Δ^∨). For l even, Δ = {e_1 − e_2, …, e_{n−1} − e_n, e_{n−1} + e_n} and Δ^∨ = {e_1^∨ − e_2^∨, …, e_{n−1}^∨ − e_n^∨, e_{n−1}^∨ + e_n^∨ − e_0^∨}. For l odd, Δ = {e_1 − e_2, …, e_{n−1} − e_n, e_n} and Δ^∨ = {e_1^∨ − e_2^∨, …, e_{n−1}^∨ − e_n^∨, 2e_n^∨ − e_0^∨}. For l ≤ 2, Δ = Δ^∨ = ∅, so GSpin_0 = GSpin_1 = GL_1 and GSpin_2 = GL_1 × GL_1. C°_{G_l} = e_0^∨(GL_1). It is the kernel of GSpin_l → SO_l, and for l > 2 it is the identity component of the centre; it is taken trivial for Sp_l and SO_l. Each standard Levi subgroup M has a fixed isomorphism i_M: M → M_β × G_{l−2r}, where β = (β_1, …, β_d) is a composition of r and 2r ≤ l. For Sp and SO, i_M(diag(a_1, …, a_d, g, a_d^*, …, a_1^*)) = (a_1, …, a_d, g). For GSpin, i_M comes from the splitting of the root datum, with the lattices of G_{l−2r} identified with span{e_0, e_{r+1}, …, e_n} and span{e_0^∨, e_{r+1}^∨, …, e_n^∨}. Υ_l is the character of GSpin_l with ⟨Υ_l, e_0^∨⟩ = 2; its kernel is Spin_l, and Υ_l is trivial for Sp and SO. Moreover Υ_l ∘ i_M^{−1}(a_1, …, a_d, g) = Υ_{l−2r}(g) ∏_{i=1}^d det(a_i). The dual groups of Sp_{2n}, SO_{2n}, SO_{2n+1}, GSpin_{2n} and GSpin_{2n+1} are SO_{2n+1}(C), SO_{2n}(C), Sp_{2n}(C), GSO_{2n}(C) and GSp_{2n}(C), and for GSpin, e_0 is the similitude character of Ĝ. For SO_{2l} and GSpin_{2l}, j is the outer involution exchanging the last two simple roots. Finally G = G_c with c > 1, and r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) is the natural embedding, with N = c + 1 if G = Sp_c and N = 2⌊c/2⌋ otherwise.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Too loose to be exact. It omits: F of characteristic 0; the explicit root datum of GSpin_l; C°_{G_l} = e_0^∨(GL_1), on which χ_π and the integral over C°_G\G depend; the normalisation ⟨Υ_l, e_0^∨⟩ = 2 ('kernel Spin_l' fixes Υ_l only up to inversion, and the normalisation enters (3.8) and the essentially tempered L-factors); the Levi formula for Υ_l, which the paper misprints as Υ_{l−2k} (see issues); and which Ĝ goes with which G.

items.statement: The γ-, L- and ε-factors of Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika and Jacquet–Shalika for pairs of irreducible admissible representations of GL_l and GL_r over a local field, defined also for non-generic representations ([JPSS83, §9.4]).

Review note on status: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 plans the GL_n × GL_m zeta integrals and gcd-normalised factors of generic representations. Its description does not include the extension to all irreducible admissible representations through Langlands data ([JPSS83, §9.4]). This paper needs that extension for arbitrary Π_ν ∈ Irr(GL_N) (§2, Theorem 3.10 with Remark 3.11, and (3.18)). Request it in AL.3; otherwise 'planned' holds only for generic pairs.

items.name: Satake parametrization of unramified representations
items.statement: An unramified π ∈ Irr(G) over a non-archimedean field is parametrized by a semisimple conjugacy class [t_π] in Ĝ.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Unramified and archimedean functorial transfer T(π)
items.statement: For unramified π over a non-archimedean field, T(π) is the unramified Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) with Satake class [r_G(t_π)]; over an archimedean field, T(π) is parametrized by r_G ∘ φ, where φ is the Langlands parameter of π ([Lan89]). The central character of T(π) is χ_π^{N/2}.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review note on status: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.4 plans only the unramified factor L(s, π, r) built from the Satake class. Nothing plans the transfer T(π) ∈ Irr(GL_N) itself or the archimedean transfer through [Lan89] (see the new coverage item on the archimedean parametrization). 'missing' is right.

items.name: Weak functorial transfer
items.statement: Let F be a number field, π an irreducible automorphic representation of G(A) and Π an irreducible automorphic representation of GL_N(A). Π is a weak functorial transfer of π if two conditions hold. First, for almost all finite places ν at which π_ν is unramified, Π_ν is the local functorial transfer T(π_ν) of π_ν dictated by r_G. Second, at every infinite place ν, the infinitesimal character of Π_ν is determined, via r_G, by that of π_ν (the infinitesimal character is encoded in the L-parameter, [NP21, Lemma 1]).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: 'Π on GL_N(A)' drops the hypothesis that Π is an irreducible automorphic representation of GL_N(A); the definition is not about arbitrary admissible Π. The item also omits that F is a number field and that π is irreducible automorphic.

items.name: Generalized Speh representations and (k, c) models
items.statement: Let F be local, k, c ≥ 1, ψ a nontrivial character of F, and ψ_k(u) = ψ(Σ_{i=1}^{k−1} tr(u_{i,i+1})) the generic character of U_(c^k) (blocks u_{i,j} ∈ Mat_c). Let τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). If τ is unitary, ρ_c(τ) is the unique irreducible quotient of Ind_{R_(k^c)}^{GL_kc}((τ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ) δ_{R_(k^c)}^{1/(2k)}), the generalized Speh representation. In general, write τ = ×_{i=1}^d |det|^{a_i} τ_i with τ_i tempered and a_1 > ⋯ > a_d, and put ρ_c(τ) = ×_{i=1}^d |det|^{a_i} ρ_c(τ_i). Then (k^c) is the unique maximal orbit in the wave-front set of ρ_c(τ), and dim Hom_{U_(c^k)}(ρ_c(τ), ψ_k) = 1 ([CFGK23, Theorem 4], [GK23, §1.4]). A finite-length admissible representation of GL_kc with these two properties is called a (k, c) representation. Fix a nonzero (k, c) functional λ. The (k, c) model W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) is the space of functions W(g) = λ(ρ_c(τ)(g)ξ), with ξ in the space of ρ_c(τ). Under right translation it is a quotient of ρ_c(τ), and for c = 1 it is the ψ_k-Whittaker model of τ.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The general definition is only alluded to ('through the Langlands data of τ'), and neither the parabolic R_(k^c) nor the character ψ_k of U_(c^k) is specified.

items.name: The local generalized doubling integral
items.statement: Let F be local, c > 1, k ≥ 1, G = G_c, H = G_{2kc}, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). Let Q = M_Q ⋉ U < H be the standard parabolic subgroup with M_Q ≅ GL_c^{k−1} × G_{2c}. For k > 1, ψ_U is a character of U that is generic for the unipotent orbit ((2k−1)^c 1^c); for k = 1, U is trivial and ψ_U = 1. The map e: G × G → St_{M_Q}(ψ_U) (into M_Q if k = 1) is injective unless G = GSpin_c, where its kernel is the diagonal copy of C°_G. Put e_1(g) = e(g, e_G) and e_2(g) = e(e_G, g). P is a standard Siegel parabolic subgroup of H and P′ = ^{j^{kc}}P. δ_0 represents the Weyl element with ^{δ_0}U_{P′} = U_P^−, δ_1 ∈ i_{M_Q}^{−1}(I_c, …, I_c, G_{2c}) ∩ U_{P′} has rank 2⌊c/2⌋, δ = δ_0δ_1, and U_0 = U ∩ U_{P′}. For k > 1 the choices satisfy ψ_U(^{δ^{−1}}u) = ψ_k^{−1}(u) for u ∈ U_(c^k). ι is an involution of G with ^δ{e(g, ^ιg)} < M_P. Explicit choices are in [CFK22, GK23], and Example 3.1 gives them for Sp_c. V(s, τ, c) is the space of Ind_P^H((|det|^{s−1/2} χ_π W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) ⊗ χ_π) ∘ i_{M_P}), realised for all s on the space of Ind_{K_H∩P}^{K_H}((χ_π W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) ⊗ χ_π) ∘ i_{M_P}). V(τ, c) is the space of entire sections f(s, h). For a matrix coefficient ω of π^∨ and f ∈ V(τ, c), Z(s, ω, f) = ∫_{C°_G\G} ∫_{U_0} ω(g) f(s, δ u_0 e_2(^ιg)) ψ_U(u_0) du_0 dg.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Calls e: G × G → St_{M_Q}(ψ_U) an embedding, but for G = GSpin_c its kernel is the diagonal copy of C°_G (which is why the integral is over C°_G\G). It also omits: the hypotheses π ∈ Irr(G), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) and ω a matrix coefficient of π^∨; the normalisation ψ_U(^{δ^{−1}}u) = ψ_k^{−1}(u) on U_(c^k); P′ = ^{j^{kc}}P; U_0 = U ∩ U_{P′}; and the space V(τ, c) of entire sections.

items.name: Basic properties of the local doubling integral
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). (1) Z(s, ω, f) converges absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0, independently of the data [CFK22, Proposition 2.5]. (2) It extends to a meromorphic function of s, which is continuous as a trilinear map on V(s, τ, c) × π × (π^ι)^∨ [CFK22, §4, §6.10]. (3) For each s there are a matrix coefficient ω and a K_H-finite f for which the integral is finite and nonzero in a neighbourhood of s [CFK22, Proposition 2.6, Corollary 6.9]. (4) Suppose F is non-archimedean, all data are normalised and unramified, K_G = G(O), K_H = H(O), du_0(U_0 ∩ K_H) = 1 and dg(K_G) = 1. Then Z(s, ω, f) = L(s, π × τ)/b(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) (3.2) [CFK22, §6.4]. Here (3.3) b(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) = [L(s + c/2, τ)] ∏_{j=1}^{c/2} L(2s + 2j − 2, τ, ∨² ⊗ χ_π) L(2s + 2j − 1, τ, ∧² ⊗ χ_π) for c even, and b(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) = ∏_{j=1}^{⌊c/2⌋} L(2s + 2j − 1, τ, ∨² ⊗ χ_π) ∏_{j=1}^{⌈c/2⌉} L(2s + 2j − 2, τ, ∧² ⊗ χ_π) for c odd. The factor L(s + c/2, τ) occurs only for G = Sp_c.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypotheses (F local, π ∈ Irr(G), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k)). It also omits the conditions of (3.2): F non-archimedean, normalised unramified data, K_G = G(O), K_H = H(O), and measures with du_0(U_0 ∩ K_H) = dg(K_G) = 1. The normalising factor b(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) of (3.3) is not written out.

items.name: Doubling γ-, L- and ε-factors
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). (a) γ(s, π × τ, ψ) is the meromorphic function such that, for all ω and f, γ(s, π × τ, ψ) Z(s, ω, f) = π(i_G)^k [γ(s, τ, ψ)] ϑ(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) Z(1 − s, ω, M*(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) f) (3.6). Here M* is the normalised intertwining operator. i_G = (−1)^{c+1} e_G, except for G = GSpin_c with c even, where i_G = i_M^{−1}(−I_{c/2}, −1) ∈ C_G for a standard Siegel Levi subgroup M. The factor γ(s, τ, ψ) occurs only for G = Sp_c. ϑ(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) = χ_π(2)^{−kn} τ(−I_k)^n τ(2I_k)^{−2n} |2|^{−2kn(s−1/2)} with n = ⌊c/2⌋ (3.7); it depends on the choices made in the construction, up to an entire nowhere-vanishing factor (Remark 3.4). Conventions: γ(s, π′ × τ, ψ) = γ(s, τ, ψ) for π′ ∈ Irr(Sp_0), and γ(s, π′ × τ, ψ) = 1 for π′ ∈ Irr(GSpin_c) with c ≤ 1 and for the trivial groups SO_0 and SO_1. (b) Let π and τ be tempered. If F is non-archimedean, L(s, π × τ) = P(q^{−s})^{−1}, where P ∈ C[X] has P(0) = 1 and the zeros of P(q^{−s}) are those of γ(s, π × τ, ψ); then ε(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π × τ, ψ) L(s, π × τ)/L(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨) (3.15), which lies in C[q^{−s}, q^s]^*. If F is archimedean, L(s, π × τ) = L(s, T(π) × τ) and ε(s, π × τ, ψ) = ε(s, T(π) × τ, ψ). (c) Let π = |Υ_c|^{r_0} π_0 and τ = |det|^{r_1} τ_0, with r_0, r_1 ∈ R, π_0 and τ_0 tempered, and r_0 = 0 unless G = GSpin_c. Then L(s, π × τ) = L(s + r_0 + r_1, π_0 × τ_0) and ε(s, π × τ, ψ) = ε(s + r_0 + r_1, π_0 × τ_0, ψ). (d) In general, write π as the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ (3.16). Here σ ∈ Irr(GL_l) is the unique irreducible quotient of ×_{i=1}^d |·|^{a_i} σ_{i,0} with σ_{i,0} tempered; π′ ∈ Irr(G_{c−2l}) has |Υ_{c−2l}|^{−r} π′ tempered, with r = 0 unless G = GSpin_c; and a_1 > ⋯ > a_d > r, with l > 0 (or l = 0 and π = π′ essentially tempered). Write τ = ×_j τ_j with each τ_j essentially tempered. Then (3.17) L(s, π × τ) = L(s, σ × τ) L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) ∏_j L(s, π′ × τ_j) and ε(s, π × τ, ψ) = ε(s, σ × τ, ψ) ε(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ, ψ) ∏_j ε(s, π′ × τ_j, ψ), with Rankin–Selberg factors for the GL pairs. (3.15) then holds in general.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The normalisation of γ is incomplete. (3.6) also carries the central value π(i_G)^k and, for Sp_c only, γ(s, τ, ψ); ϑ is not written out; the conventions for groups of rank ≤ 0 are missing (the paper itself omits SO_0 and SO_1, see issues); and ε is not defined. The Langlands-quotient clause needs the conditions of (3.16). Read correctly these are a_d > r (the printed a_d > r/2 is a misprint), with l = 0 allowed for essentially tempered π (see issues).

items.name: Characterization of the doubling γ-factor
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). The factor γ(s, π × τ, ψ) of (3.6) satisfies the following properties and is characterised by them [CFK22, Theorem 4.2], in the GSpin conventions of Remark 3.6. (i) Unramified twisting (3.8): for G ≠ GSpin_c, γ(s, π × |det|^{s_1} τ, ψ) = γ(s + s_1, π × τ, ψ); for G = GSpin_c, γ(s, |Υ_c|^{s_0} π × |det|^{s_1} τ, ψ) = γ(s + s_0 + s_1, π × τ, ψ), for all s_0, s_1 ∈ C. (ii) Multiplicativity. If π is a quotient of (σ_1 × ⋯ × σ_d) ⋊ π′ with the σ_i and π′ irreducible admissible, then γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π′ × τ, ψ) ∏_{i=1}^d γ(s, σ_i × τ, ψ) γ(s, σ_i^∨ × χ_π τ, ψ) (3.9), with Rankin–Selberg factors for the GL pairs. If τ is a quotient of ×_{i=1}^{d′} τ_i with each τ_i irreducible and generic, then γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = ∏_i γ(s, π × τ_i, ψ) (3.10). (iii) If all data are unramified, γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = L(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨)/L(s, π × τ). (iv) Duality: γ(s, π^∨ × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π × χ_π^{−1} τ, ψ). (v) Functional equation: γ(s, π × τ, ψ) γ(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨, ψ^{−1}) = 1 (3.11). (vi) For b ∈ F^* and ψ_b(x) = ψ(bx), γ(s, π × τ, ψ_b) = χ_π^{k⌊c/2⌋}(b) τ(bI_k)^N |b|^{kN(s−1/2)} γ(s, π × τ, ψ) (3.12). (vii) If F is archimedean, γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = ε(s, T(π) × τ, ψ) L(1 − s, T(π)^∨ × τ^∨)/L(s, T(π) × τ) (3.13). (viii) Crude functional equation. Let F_0 be a number field, ψ = ⊗ψ_ν a nontrivial character of A/F_0, π = ⊗π_ν and τ = ⊗τ_ν irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations of G(A) and GL_k(A), and S a finite set of places outside which all data are unramified. Then L^S(s, π × τ) = ∏_{ν∈S} γ(s, π_ν × τ_ν, ψ_ν) L^S(1 − s, π^∨ × τ^∨) (3.14).
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Theorem 4.2]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The properties are cited only by equation number, so the GSpin-specific normalisations are never stated. These are: twisting by |Υ_c|^{s_0}; the factor γ(s, σ_i^∨ × χ_π τ) in multiplicativity (which differs from [CFK22], Remark 3.6); duality with χ_π^{−1}; and the ψ-dependence χ_π^{k⌊c/2⌋}(b) τ(bI_k)^N |b|^{kN(s−1/2)}.

items.name: Compatibility with the unramified and archimedean transfer
items.statement: For π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), with π unramified if F is non-archimedean, the γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × τ and T(π) × τ coincide.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Lemma 7.1] in the non-archimedean case; (3.13) otherwise; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Holomorphy of tempered L-factors
items.statement: For tempered π ∈ Irr(G) (unramified if F is non-archimedean) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k): if τ is tempered, L(s, π × τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) > 0; if τ is unitary, it is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Corollary 7.2]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Poles of L(s, π × τ) in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 for a Langlands quotient
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), with τ and χ_π unitary, and π unramified if F is non-archimedean. Write π as the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ as in (3.16), with l > 0. Then L(s, π × τ)/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) is holomorphic and nowhere zero in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Omits that τ is generic (τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k)) and that π ∈ Irr(G), F local.

items.name: Stability of γ-factors
items.statement: Over a non-archimedean F, let π ∈ Irr(G) and Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) with central character χ_π^{N/2}. If η is a sufficiently highly ramified character (depending on π and Π), then for every unramified τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) the γ-, L- and ε-factors of π × ητ and Π × ητ coincide, and L(s, π × ητ) = L(s, Π × ητ) = 1.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Lemma 7.3]; Remark 3.11 removes the unramified and generic assumptions on Π; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Coarse transfer
items.statement: Let F be a local field and π ∈ Irr(G). Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) is a coarse transfer of π if γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, Π × τ, ψ) (Rankin–Selberg on the right) for every k ≥ 1 and every τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) (3.18). By (3.10) and the multiplicativity of Rankin–Selberg γ-factors, it suffices to check supercuspidal τ. If π is unramified or F is archimedean, T(π) is a coarse transfer of π (Theorem 3.7).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The doubling γ-factor γ(s, π × τ, ψ) is defined, by (3.6), only for generic τ. The item follows the paper's misprint (see issues) and quantifies over all τ ∈ Irr(GL_k). It also omits that F is local.

items.name: Gauge bound for (k, c) Whittaker functions
items.statement: For τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), k > 1, there is d_0 > 0 such that for every W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) there is φ ∈ S(Mat_c) with |W(diag(g, I_(k−1)c))| ≤ |det g|^{−d_0} φ(g) for all g ∈ GL_c.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Archimedean bounds for (k, c) functionals
items.statement: Over an archimedean field there are d_0 > 0 and a continuous seminorm γ with |λ(ρ_c(τ)(ugo)ξ)| ≤ γ(ξ)|τ((det g_k)I_k)| ∏_{i<k} |det(g_k^{−1}g_i)|^{−d_0} for g = diag(g_1, …, g_k), and, for each ξ, the refined bound (3.20) with Schwartz functions φ_i of g_{i+1}^{−1}g_i.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The functional T and descent from (k, c) to (k, l) models
items.statement: Let F be local and k > 1. Let R < G be the standard maximal parabolic subgroup of (3.16), with M_R ≅ GL_l × G_{c−2l}, 0 < l ≤ n = ⌊c/2⌋. Identify U_R with Mat_{l×(n−l)} × Mat_{l×(c−n−l)} × C_{U_R}, and put S^lin(U_R) = S(Mat_{l×(n−l)}) ⊗ S(Mat_{l×(c−n−l)}) ⊗ S(C_{U_R}). For z ∈ U_R, let r_z ∈ diag(U_(l,c−2l,l) ∩ U_(l,c−n−l,n), I_{(k−1)c}) be defined by (3.23). For a ∈ GL_l, put m_a = diag(a, I_{kc−l}) and m′_a = diag(a, I_{(k−1)l}). Assume τ ∈ Irr_gen,u(GL_k). For W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) and μ ∈ S^lin(U_R), the integral T(W, μ) = ∫_{U_R} W(r_z) μ(z) dz (3.25) converges absolutely and defines a continuous functional on W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) ⊗ S^lin(U_R). Moreover, the map a ↦ T(m_a·W ⊗ μ) on GL_l is a surjection onto the space of functions a ↦ W_l(m′_a), where W_l ranges over |det|^{(kc−kl−c+l)/2} W_ψ(ρ_l(τ)).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to Lemma 3.16, but the standing notation it depends on is not stated: k > 1; the parabolic R of (3.16); S^lin(U_R); r_z (3.23); m_a and m′_a. It also leaves out that, by the twist of E1, the lemma extends to τ = χτ_0 with χ a quasi-character and τ_0 unitary.

items.name: The GL_l × GL_k reduction integral Z^2
items.statement: Let F be local, k > 1, σ ∈ Irr(GL_l) (unramified if F is non-archimedean), τ ∈ Irr_gen,u(GL_k), and χ a quasi-character of F^* (in the application χ = χ_π). For a matrix coefficient ω_l of σ^∨, W ∈ χ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) = W_ψ(ρ_c(χτ)), φ ∈ S(Mat_l) and μ ∈ S^lin(U_R), put Z^2(s, ω_l, W, φ, μ) = ∫_{GL_l} ∫_{U_R} ω_l(a) W(r_z m_a) μ(z) φ(a) |det a|^{s − (kc − c − l + 1)/2} dz da (3.32). This integral converges absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0, independently of the data. It continues meromorphically to a form that is continuous on V_σ × V_σ^∨ × χ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) × S(Mat_l) × S^lin(U_R). For each s there are data with φ ∈ S_c(Mat_l) and μ ∈ S_c^lin(U_R) such that Z^2(s, ω_l, W, φ, μ)/L(s, σ^∨ × χτ) is nonzero at s. The paper's proof covers unitary χ. For χ = |·|^r χ_0 with χ_0 unitary, the case χ at s is the case χ_0 at s + r (E1).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The integral (3.32) is cited only by number, and the standing assumption k > 1 is missing. χ_π is not quantified: Proposition 3.17 is stated before π is fixed, and it is later applied with the χ_π of an arbitrary π ∈ Irr_rel(G). The proof as printed covers only unitary χ_π (E1, confirmed); the statement for any quasi-character needs the twist repair.

items.name: Z^1 as an integral over the open cell
items.statement: When absolutely convergent, Z^1(s, ω, f) of (3.40) equals the integral (3.41) over U_R × C°_G\U_{R′}R′^− × U_R^− × U_0 × GL_l, through an open embedding U into U_{P′} that is a homeomorphism (diffeomorphism) onto its image.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Nonvanishing of Z^1 modulo L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ)
items.statement: Let F be local, k > 1, π ∈ Irr_rel(G) written as the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ as in (3.16), and τ ∈ Irr_gen,u(GL_k). For every s_0 ∈ C there are φ, φ^∨ and f ∈ V(τ, c) with the following properties: Z^1(s, ω^{e_G}_{φ,φ^∨}, f) of (3.40) converges absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0, continues meromorphically, and Z^1(s, ω^{e_G}_{φ,φ^∨}, f)/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) is nonzero at s_0. For non-unitary χ_π this uses the twisted form of Proposition 3.17 (E1).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). See finding E1 on the unitarity of χ_π. Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the standing assumption k > 1: the proof passes through Proposition 3.17 and Appendix A, which need k > 1. For π ∈ Irr_rel(G) with non-unitary χ_π (possible only for GSpin_c), the statement holds only with the twist repair of Proposition 3.17 (E1, confirmed).

items.name: Archimedean convergence of the unfolded integrals
items.statement: Over an archimedean field, (3.39) and Z^1 converge absolutely in Re(s) ≫ 0 independently of the data and are continuous in ϕ, ϕ^∨ and f.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Nonvanishing of Z modulo L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ)
items.statement: Let F be local, k > 1, π ∈ Irr_rel(G) written as in (3.16), and τ ∈ Irr_gen,u(GL_k). For every s ∈ C there are a matrix coefficient ω of π^∨ and f ∈ V(τ, c) such that Z(s, ω, f)/L(s, σ^∨ × χ_π τ) is nonzero at s. For non-unitary χ_π this uses the twisted form of Proposition 3.17 (E1).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). See finding E1 on the unitarity of χ_π. Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the standing assumption k > 1 (the proof goes through Proposition 3.19). For non-unitary χ_π, the statement relies on the twist repair of E1 (confirmed).

items.name: Convergence of intertwining integrals against smooth vectors
items.statement: Let F be R or C, and let 𝒢 be a split connected reductive group as in §1, with maximal compact subgroup K_𝒢 orthogonal to T_𝒢 for the Killing form. Let R < 𝒢 be a standard parabolic subgroup, A_R the identity component of C_{M_R}, a* = X(A_R) ⊗ R, and V_R^𝒢(ν, σ) the space of Ind_R^𝒢(σ ⊗ e^{⟨ν, H_{M_R}(·)⟩}) for ν ∈ a*_C. Let σ ∈ Irr(M_R) be tempered, with invariant inner product ⟨,⟩_σ on its space V_σ, and let Re(ν) lie in the positive Weyl chamber of a* with respect to R. Then ∫_{U_R^−} |⟨φ(u), w⟩_σ| du < ∞ for every φ ∈ V_R^𝒢(ν, σ) and every smooth w ∈ V_σ, and (φ, w) ↦ ∫_{U_R^−} ⟨φ(u), w⟩_σ du is continuous.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Lemma 3.22 is archimedean only (𝒢 defined over R or C, with K_𝒢 orthogonal to T_𝒢 for the Killing form). The item omits this and writes 'ν in the positive chamber' where the lemma assumes Re(ν) in the positive Weyl chamber, ν ∈ a*_C. Review note on status: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1 builds the smooth Fréchet globalisations this lemma works in, but it does not plan Sun's bound or Wallach's convergence estimate (see the new coverage item). 'missing' is right.

items.name: Local poles are attained by the doubling integral
items.statement: Let F be a local field, π ∈ Irr_rel,a.u.(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen,u(GL_k), k ≥ 1. Here π is unramified if F is non-archimedean, arbitrary if F is archimedean, and in both cases χ_π is unitary. For each s with Re(s) ≥ 1/2 there are a matrix coefficient ω of π^∨ and a K_H-finite f ∈ V(τ, c) such that the meromorphic function Z(s, ω, f)/L(s, π × τ) is nonzero at s; it may have a pole there. The case k > 1 is proved in §3.6; the case k = 1 is quoted from [Yam14, Theorem 7.1].
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Should say that the quotient may have a pole at s. The paper adds '(but may have a pole)': 'nonzero at s' means the Laurent expansion at s has a nonzero leading term. The item also lists prerequisites that cover only k > 1. For k = 1 the paper refers to [Yam14, Theorem 7.1] 'with minor adjustments' (Yamana treats O_c, not SO_c or GSpin_c); that input needs its own item (see coverage). Review note on status: Add the k = 1 input (the new coverage item 'Theorem 3.12 for k = 1') as a prerequisite; the listed prerequisites (via Z-over-sigma) cover only k > 1.

items.name: Converse Theorem of Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi
items.statement: Let Π = ⊗′Π_ν be irreducible admissible on GL_N(A) with central character trivial on F^* and L(s, Π) absolutely convergent in Re(s) ≫ 0. If for every τ ∈ A(S, η) the L-function L(s, Π × τ) is nice (entire with L(s, Π^∨ × τ^∨), bounded in vertical strips, and satisfying L(s, Π × τ) = ε(s, Π × τ)L(1 − s, Π^∨ × τ^∨)), there is an irreducible automorphic Π′ of GL_N(A) with Π′_ν ≅ Π_ν for all ν ∉ S.
items.note: Cited from [CKPSS01, §2]; A(S, η) is the set of η-twists of unitary cuspidal τ′ of GL_k(A), 1 ≤ k < N, unramified at the nonempty finite set S of finite places. Review note on status: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.5 plans only the GL_2 converse theorem. The GL_N theorem of [CKPSS01, §2], with η-twists, S nonempty and 1 ≤ k ≤ N − 1, is planned nowhere, so 'missing' is right. missing is correct. The atlas plans only the GL_2 converse theorem (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.5). The GL_N theorem of [CPS94, CPS99], in the eta-twisted form of [CKPSS01, §2], is planned nowhere. The facts from [CPS94, Lemmas 2.1-2.2] that the statement needs are a proposed new item (coverage).

items.name: The Eisenstein series E_{τ,θ,c}
items.statement: Let F be a number field, c >= 1, k >= 1, H = G_2kc (Sp, SO or GSpin, split, of the same type as G), and P a standard Siegel parabolic of H, M_P ≅ GL_kc × G_0 via i_{M_P}. Let τ be a cuspidal representation of GL_k(A), and ρ_c(τ) the generalized Speh representation of GL_kc(A) attached to τ ([Jac84, §2.4]). Let θ be a unitary Hecke character of A^* when H = GSpin_2kc, and θ = 1 otherwise. Let K_H = ∏_ν K_{H_ν} be maximal compact in good position ([MW95, I.1.1, I.1.4]). For an entire K_H-finite section f of Ind_{P(A)}^{H(A)}((|det|^s ρ_c(τ) ⊗ θ)∘i_{M_P}), set E_{τ,θ,c}(h; s, f) = Σ_{γ ∈ P(F)\H(F)} f(s, γh), h ∈ H(A). The series converges absolutely for Re(s) >> 0 and continues meromorphically to C ([Lan76, MW95]).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: θ is used but not introduced. It is a unitary Hecke character of A^*, present only when H = GSpin_2kc, and θ = 1 otherwise; Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.4 use its unitarity. The construction is for every c >= 1, since c = 1 starts the induction in Theorem 4.1 and c' = c - 1 recurs. ρ_c(τ) here is the global generalized Speh representation of [Jac84, §2.4], not the local one of item speh; no item covers it (see coverage). Review note on status: missing is correct. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1-AS.2 plan Eisenstein series of cuspidal data; this series is induced from the residual Speh representation, which only ET.7a (the GL_m residual spectrum) touches.

items.name: Holomorphy of the intertwining operators M_1 and M_2
items.statement: Let τ be a unitary cuspidal representation of GL_k(A) and θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H = GSpin_2kc), with |det|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all t ∈ R. Let c >= 2 and c' = c - 1. Let M_0(s): |det|^s τ ⋊ θ → |det|^{-s}θτ^∨ ⋊ θ be the standard intertwining operator for the Siegel parabolic of G_2k(A); for H = SO_2kc or GSpin_2kc with k odd, the target is induced from ^ȷP, (4.8). Put M_1(s) = M_0(s + c'/2): |det|^{s+c'/2}τ ⋊ θ → |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ ⋊ θ. Let M_2(s): |det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) × |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ → |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ × |det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) be the standard intertwining operator on GL_kc(A). Then M_1(s) is holomorphic in Re(s) > -c'/2, and M_2(s) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The item defines neither operator and states no hypothesis. Lemma 4.3 lies inside the proof of Theorem 4.1 and uses its hypotheses. The M_1 part rests on [MW95, Rem. IV.3.12], which needs |det|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨. The M_2 part needs the same hypothesis on the line Re(s) = 1/2, although the printed proof does not say so and argues the step backwards (see the new issue on the proof of Lemma 4.3).

items.name: Shape of the cuspidal exponents
items.statement: Let τ be a unitary cuspidal representation of GL_k(A), θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H = GSpin_2kc), and c >= 1. For s ∈ C, let E_{s,c} be the leading coefficient of the Laurent expansion of E_{τ,θ,c}(·; s', f) about s' = s. Let e(s,c) be the set of real parts of the cuspidal exponents of E_{s,c} along P_{(k^c)} ([MW95, I.3.3, I.3.5]). Write them in the standard basis of the character lattice of M_{P_{(k^c)}} ≅ GL_k^c (× GL_1 when H = GSpin_2kc, whose coordinate is 0 because θ is unitary), so e(s,c) ⊂ R^c. Then every e ∈ e(s,c) has the form e = Re(s)(a_1, ..., a_c) + (b_1, ..., b_c), with a_j = ±1 and Σ_{i<=j} b_i <= 0 for all 1 <= j <= c.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Hypotheses and definitions are missing. τ must be unitary cuspidal and θ unitary: the real parts are read off using this, and the extra GSpin coordinate vanishes because θ is unitary. c >= 1. e(s,c) is defined for every s through the leading Laurent coefficient.

items.name: Holomorphy of the Eisenstein series
items.statement: For τ unitary cuspidal on GL_k(A) and θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H = GSpin_2kc), if |·|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all real t, then E_{τ,θ,c}(h; s, f) is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 0.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: The global doubling integral and its Eulerian form
items.statement: Let c > 1, k >= 1, G = G_c, H = G_2kc. Let P, Q, U = U_Q be as in §3.3, ψ_U the character of U(F)\U(A) generic for the orbit ((2k-1)^c 1^c), and e: G(A) × G(A) → St_{M_Q(A)}(ψ_U), whose kernel is the diagonal C°_G(A). Take K_H with e_ν(K_{G_ν}, K_{G_ν}) < K_{H_ν} for all ν. Let π and τ be cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A), and E(h; s, f) = E_{χ_πτ, χ_π, c}(h; s, f) (θ = χ_π) for an entire K_H-finite section f of Ind_{P(A)}^{H(A)}((|det|^s χ_π ρ_c(τ) ⊗ χ_π)∘i_{M_P}). Put E^{U,ψ_U}(h; s, f) = ∫_{U(F)\U(A)} E(uh; s, f)ψ_U(u) du. For cusp forms ϕ_1 of π and ϕ_2 of π^∨, set Z(s, ϕ_1, ϕ_2, f) = ∫_{(C°_G(A)G(F) × C°_G(A)G(F))\G(A)×G(A)} ϕ_1(g_1) ^ιϕ_2(g_2) E^{U,ψ_U}(e(g_1, g_2); s - 1/2, f) dg_1 dg_2, where ^ιϕ_2(g) = ϕ_2(ιgι^{-1}). The integral converges absolutely wherever E(·; s - 1/2, f) is holomorphic, so it is meromorphic on C and holomorphic away from the poles of E(·; s - 1/2, f). For decomposable data and Re(s) >> 0, Z(s, ϕ_1, ϕ_2, f) = ∏_ν Z(s, ω_ν, f_ν), with ω_ν a matrix coefficient of π_ν^∨ and f_ν ∈ V(τ_ν, c) ([GK23, §3.2]). Hence, for a sufficiently large finite set S of places and as meromorphic functions, b^S(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) Z(s, ϕ_1, ϕ_2, f) = L^S(s, π × τ) ∏_{ν∈S} Z(s, ω_ν, f_ν) (4.10), where b^S = ∏_{ν∉S} b(s, c, τ_ν ⊗ χ_{π_ν}) with b as in (3.3).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits three things. First, which Eisenstein series enters: E = E_{χ_πτ, χ_π, c} (θ = χ_π) on Ind((|det|^s χ_π ρ_c(τ) ⊗ χ_π)∘i_{M_P}), evaluated at s - 1/2; this is what lets Theorem 4.1 apply to χ_πτ in Theorem 4.8. Second, the absolute convergence of Z wherever the Eisenstein series is holomorphic, which gives holomorphy away from its poles and is used in Theorem 4.8. Third, the unfolding Z = ∏_ν Z(s, ω_ν, f_ν) ([GK23, §3.2]), which produces (4.10).

items.name: The completed L-function L(s, π × τ)
items.statement: Let π and τ be cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A), and ψ = ⊗'ψ_ν a nontrivial character of F\A. Then L(s, π × τ) = ∏_ν L(s, π_ν × τ_ν), over all places of F, is a meromorphic function, and ε(s, π × τ) = ∏_ν ε(s, π_ν × τ_ν, ψ_ν), with the local factors of §3.4 ((3.15)-(3.17)).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Hypotheses missing. π and τ are cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A), ψ is a fixed nontrivial character of F\A, and the products run over all places, archimedean ones included. The paper records that the product is a meromorphic function.

items.name: Global functional equation
items.statement: Let c > 1, k >= 1, and let π and τ be cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A). Then L(s, π × τ) = ε(s, π × τ) L(1 - s, π^∨ × τ^∨) as meromorphic functions, with the completed L and ε of §4.3.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Theorem 8.3]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: No hypotheses are stated. [CFK22, Theorem 8.3], as quoted in §4.3, is for cuspidal π of G(A) and τ of GL_k(A), not necessarily unitary, as an identity of meromorphic functions.

items.name: Boundedness in vertical strips
items.statement: Let π and τ be cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A). If L(s, π × τ) and L(1 - s, π^∨ × τ^∨) are entire, they are bounded in vertical strips of finite width.
items.note: Cited from [CFK22, Corollary 8.5]; the paper uses it as an input. G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: No hypotheses are stated. Theorem 4.7 is for cuspidal π of G(A) and τ of GL_k(A).

items.name: Entireness of twisted L-functions
items.statement: Let π and τ be unitary cuspidal on G(A) and GL_k(A) with (1) |·|^{it}χ_π τ ≇ τ^∨ for all real t, and (2) L(s, π_ν × τ_ν) = L(s, π_ν^∨ × τ_ν^∨) = 1 at every finite ν where π_ν is not unramified. Then L(s, π × τ) and L(s, π^∨ × τ^∨) are entire and bounded in vertical strips of finite width.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Weak functorial transfer of cuspidal representations
items.statement: Every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation π of G(A) has a weak functorial transfer Π to GL_N(A); the proof yields one with Π_∞ the archimedean transfer of π_∞ (Remark 4.9).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Weak transfers are coarse transfers everywhere
items.statement: If Π is a weak functorial transfer of a cuspidal π of G(A), then Π_ν is a coarse transfer of π_ν at every place ν.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c).

items.name: Existence of local coarse transfers
items.statement: Let f be a local field of characteristic 0. Every π' ∈ Irr(G(f)) has a coarse transfer Π ∈ Irr(GL_N(f)) in the sense of (3.18).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The field must have characteristic 0: this is the paper's standing convention (§1), and the proof globalizes through a number field.

items.name: The GL_c × GL_k integrals of Appendix A
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, c >= 1, k > 1, π ∈ Irr(GL_c), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) the (k,c) model, and e_1(g) = diag(g, I_{(k-1)c}). For a matrix coefficient ω of π and W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)), set Z(s, ω, W) = ∫_{GL_c} W(e_1(g)) ω(g) |det g|^{s-(kc-2c+1)/2} dg. The Schwartz function of the general integral Z(s, ω, W, φ) can be dropped because k > 1. Set Z*(s, ω, W) = ∫_{GL_c} ∫_{U^-_{((k-2)c,c)}} W(diag(I_{(k-1)c}, g) diag(I_c, z) w_{((k-1)c,c)}) ω(g) |det g|^{s-1+(kc-2c+1)/2} dz dg, where w_{(a,b)} = [[0, I_a], [I_b, 0]]. Z converges absolutely in a right half-plane and Z* in a left half-plane, independently of the data; both lie in the space of Theorem A.1. Hence, given meromorphic continuation, there is a meromorphic, not identically zero γ(s, π × τ, ψ) with γ(s, π × τ, ψ) Z(s, ω, W) = π(-1)^{k-1} Z*(s, ω, W) for all ω and W (A.3). When c = 1, γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ^RS(s, π × τ, ψ).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42). Also: Z* is not written out. Z converges in a right half-plane and Z* in a left half-plane. γ exists only given the meromorphic continuation, which the appendix proves for π unramified or F archimedean (τ unitary), and over non-archimedean F for all π and generic τ by Bernstein's principle. For c = 1, γ = γ^RS ([Sou93, (11.7.1)]).

items.name: Uniqueness of the trilinear forms
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, c >= 1, k > 1, π ∈ Irr(GL_c), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). Let U^⊘_{(c^k)} = {u ∈ U_{(c^k)} : u_{1,2} = 0} and ψ^⊘ = ψ_k|U^⊘_{(c^k)}, e_1(g) = diag(g, I_{(k-1)c}), e_2(g) = diag(I_c, g, ..., g). Except for finitely many values of q^{-s} (F non-archimedean), or a discrete set of s (F archimedean), the space of continuous trilinear forms B on π × π^∨ × ρ_c(τ) with B(π(g)ϕ, τ^∨(det g')π^∨(g')ϕ^∨, ρ_c(τ)(u e_1(g) e_2(g'))ξ) = ψ^⊘(u) |det g g'^{-1}|^{-s+(kc-2c+1)/2} B(ϕ, ϕ^∨, ξ) for all g, g' ∈ GL_c and u ∈ U^⊘_{(c^k)} has dimension at most one ([Kap23, Theorem 25]).
items.note: Cited from [Kap23, Theorem 25]. Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Hypotheses missing: F local of characteristic 0, π ∈ Irr(GL_c), τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k), and k > 1 (the appendix fixes k > 1 just before Theorem A.1). The equivariance (A.2) is cited only by number.

items.name: Multiplicativity of the appendix γ-factor
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, k > 1, τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) unitary, c >= 2, 0 < l < c, R = R_{(l,c-l)} < GL_c, and σ = π_1 ⊗ π_2 ∈ Irr(M_R), with π_1 ∈ Irr(GL_l) and π_2 ∈ Irr(GL_{c-l}). If π ∈ Irr(GL_c) and π ⊂ Ind_R^{GL_c}(σ), then γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ(s, π_1 × τ, ψ) γ(s, π_2 × τ, ψ). Hence, if π is unramified (F non-archimedean) or F is archimedean, γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = γ^RS(s, π × τ, ψ).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42). Also missing: τ unitary and k > 1. From p. 44 on the appendix assumes 'Henceforth also assume τ is unitary', because the proof uses the realization (A.4)-(A.5) of [CFGK23, §3.2].

items.name: The appendix L-factor
items.statement: Standing assumptions (p. 50): F is local of characteristic 0; c >= 1, k > 1; π ∈ Irr(GL_c), unramified if F is non-archimedean (any π if F is archimedean); τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) unitary. Let F be the ring of entire functions (C[q^{-s}, q^s] if F is non-archimedean), M its fraction field, and F^* its units. There is a nowhere vanishing fraktur-L(s, π × τ) ∈ M such that fraktur-L(s, π × τ)^{-1} Z(s, ω, W) ∈ F for all ω and W, and for each s some data make this quotient nonzero at s. If F is non-archimedean, fraktur-L = P(q^{-s})^{-1} with P ∈ C[X], P(0) = 1. If F is archimedean, fraktur-L is unique up to F^*. Moreover: (1) fraktur-L(s, π × τ) is equally the gcd of the integrals Z*(1 - s, ω', W'), for ω' a matrix coefficient of π^∨ and W' ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ^∨)). (2) In the setting of Theorem A.2, fraktur-L(s, π × τ) = A(s) fraktur-L(s, π_1 × τ) fraktur-L(s, π_2 × τ) with A ∈ F. (3) fraktur-L is independent of ψ. (4) fraktur-L(s, |det|^{s_0}π × τ) = fraktur-L(s, π × |det|^{s_0}τ) = fraktur-L(s + s_0, π × τ).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42). The appendix writes this factor as fraktur L, not L, and keeps L(s, π × τ) for the Rankin–Selberg factor (p. 54). The item's plain 'L' clashes with that convention, and the clash inverted the gl-RS-divides item. 'Multiplicative up to entire factors' needs a direction: fraktur-L(π) = A · fraktur-L(π_1) fraktur-L(π_2) with A entire. Also omitted: the normalisation P(0) = 1, uniqueness up to F^* over archimedean fields, and k > 1.

items.name: L-factors of Langlands quotients
items.statement: Under the standing assumptions of Theorem A.6, let π be the unique irreducible quotient of Ind_{R_β}^{GL_c}(σ_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ σ_d), where β = (β_1, ..., β_d), d >= 2, σ_i = |det|^{a_i}σ_{i,0} with σ_{i,0} ∈ Irr(GL_{β_i}) tempered and a_1 > ... > a_d. Let π' be the unique irreducible quotient of Ind_{R_{β'}}^{GL_{c-β_1}}(σ_2 ⊗ ... ⊗ σ_d). Then fraktur-L(s, π' × τ) = P(s) fraktur-L(s, π × τ) with P ∈ F. So every pole of fraktur-L(s, π' × τ), with multiplicity, is a pole of fraktur-L(s, π × τ).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42). Missing: the standing assumptions (π unramified or F archimedean, τ unitary generic, k > 1), the Langlands data (σ_{i,0} tempered, a_1 > ... > a_d, d >= 2), and the fact that the factors are the appendix gcds fraktur-L.

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg factor divides the appendix L-factor
items.statement: Under the standing assumptions of Theorem A.6 (F local of characteristic 0; π ∈ Irr(GL_c), unramified if F is non-archimedean; τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) unitary; k > 1), let L(s, π × τ) be the Rankin–Selberg factor of [JPSS83, JS90], defined through the Langlands data of π when π is not generic. Then fraktur-L(s, π × τ)^{-1} L(s, π × τ) ∈ F. That is, L(s, π × τ)/fraktur-L(s, π × τ) is entire, and every pole of the Rankin–Selberg factor, with multiplicity, is a pole of the gcd fraktur-L(s, π × τ).
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: Inverted. Proposition A.10 (p. 54) reads 'fraktur-L(s, π × τ)^{-1} L(s, π × τ) ∈ F', where fraktur-L is the gcd of Theorem A.6 and L is the Rankin–Selberg factor. So L^RS / fraktur-L is entire: every Rankin–Selberg pole is a pole of the gcd. The item says L^RS^{-1} · (appendix factor) is entire, which the paper neither proves nor uses. The proof gives only fraktur-L = A · L^RS with A nowhere vanishing but possibly with poles, which is why Theorem A.11 allows Z/L^RS a pole. The standing hypotheses are also missing. The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg poles are attained by the GL_c × GL_k integrals
items.statement: Let F be a local field of characteristic 0, c >= 1, k > 1, π ∈ Irr(GL_c) (unramified if F is non-archimedean), and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) unitary. For each s ∈ C there are a matrix coefficient ω of π and W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) such that Z(s, ω, W)/L(s, π × τ) is nonzero at s, possibly with a pole there; L is the Rankin–Selberg factor. If F is archimedean, ω can be taken K_{GL_c}-finite and W K_{GL_kc}-finite.
items.note: G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c, split over F (c > 1), r_G: Ĝ → GL_N(C) its standard representation (N = c + 1 for Sp_c, otherwise 2⌊c/2⌋), and χ_π the restriction of the central character to C°_G (trivial unless G = GSpin_c). Review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24): statement corrected against the paper: The item says the quotient is 'nonzero at s'. Theorem A.11 says 'nonzero (but may have a pole)': Z/fraktur-L is entire, but fraktur-L/L^RS may have poles. 'Finite' should read: ω K_{GL_c}-finite and W K_{GL_kc}-finite. The shared note ('G = G_c is Sp_c, SO_c or GSpin_c ... c > 1') is wrong for Appendix A, where G = GL_c with c >= 1 ('except here G is a general linear group', p. 42).

items.name: The quasi-character χ_π
items.statement: Let F be local. For an admissible representation π of GSpin_l with a central character, χ_π is the quasi-character x ↦ π(e_0^∨(x)) of F^*; this is essentially π restricted to C°_{GSpin_l} = e_0^∨(GL_1). For G_l ≠ GSpin_l, χ_π^d is trivial for every d ∈ ½Z. If (σ ⊗ π) ∘ i_{M_R} ∈ Irr(M_R), then χ_{σ⋊π} = χ_π. Globally, for an irreducible automorphic representation π of GSpin_c(A), χ_π is the Hecke character of A^* obtained by the same pullback; for G ≠ GSpin_c, χ_π = 1. Since ⟨Υ_c, e_0^∨⟩ = 2, χ_{|Υ_c|^{s_0} π} = |·|^{2s_0} χ_π.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): χ_π enters V(s, τ, c), the γ-factor, the L-factor (3.17), Corollary 3.9, all of §3.6 and E1, but no item defines it; it appears only in the shared notes. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Multiplicity one for the generalized doubling integrals
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr(G) and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). By [CFK22, Proposition 2.2] and Theorem 3.2(2), Z(s, ω, f) defines an element of Hom_{U ⋊ e(G,G)}(V(s, τ, c), ψ_U^{−1} ⊗ π^∨ ⊗ π^ι) (3.4). This space has dimension at most 1, except for finitely many values of q^{−s} if F is non-archimedean and a discrete set of s if F is archimedean [GK23, Theorem 2.1].
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §3.4, p. 14, (3.4), citing [GK23, Theorem 2.1] and [CFK22, Proposition 2.2]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): This theorem is what makes (3.6) define γ(s, π × τ, ψ). It is quoted from [GK23, Theorem 2.1] with [CFK22, Proposition 2.2], and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: The normalised intertwining operator M*(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ)
items.statement: Let w_P ∈ H represent 𝔴_H 𝔴_{M_P}. The standard intertwining operator M(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, w_P) maps V(s, τ, c) to V(1 − s, χ_π^{−1} τ^∨, c); the (k, c) models on both sides are taken with respect to ψ, and for kc odd the target is induced from ^jP and (|det|^{1/2−s} W_ψ(ρ_c(τ^∨)) ⊗ χ_π) ∘ i_{^jM_P}. V(s, τ, c) has a unique degenerate Whittaker model [CFK22, Theorem 3.2], with functional λ(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) depending on δ_0 and δ_1 [CFK22, (3.3)]. There is a meromorphic C(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) such that λ(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) f = C(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) λ(1 − s, c, χ_π^{−1} τ^∨ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) M(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, w_P) f for all f ∈ V(τ, c) (3.5), modified for kc odd as in [CFK22, §3]. Then M*(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) = C(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, ψ) M(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π, w_P), and Z(1 − s, ω, M* f) converges absolutely in a left half plane.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): local-factors uses M* by name only. M*, the degenerate Whittaker functional and its uniqueness [CFK22, Theorem 3.2], and the factor C of (3.5) form a construction of their own. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Langlands classification for G_c and the realisation by intertwining integrals
items.statement: Let F be local. Every π ∈ Irr(G) is either essentially tempered (π = |Υ_c|^{r_0} π_0 with π_0 tempered) or the unique irreducible quotient of σ ⋊ π′ = Ind_R^G((σ ⊗ π′) ∘ i_{M_R}) for a standard maximal parabolic subgroup R with M_R ≅ GL_l × G_{c−2l}, l > 0. Here σ is the unique irreducible quotient of ×_{i=1}^d |·|^{a_i} σ_{i,0} with σ_{i,0} tempered, π′ ∈ Irr(G_{c−2l}) with |Υ_{c−2l}|^{−r} π′ tempered, and a_1 > ⋯ > a_d > r (r = 0 unless G = GSpin_c). Put ε = σ ⊗ π′. Then π is isomorphic to the image of I: Ind_R^G(ε ∘ i_{M_R}) → Ind_{R^−}^G(ε ∘ i_{M_R}), I(φ)(g) = ∫_{U_R^−} φ(yg) dy. This integral converges absolutely: over non-archimedean F against K-finite vectors [Wal03, §IV.1], [Wal88, §5], and over archimedean F against all smooth vectors (Lemma 3.22). π^∨ is the Langlands quotient of Ind_{R^−}^G(ε^∨ ∘ i_{M_R}), is contained in Ind_R^G(ε^∨ ∘ i_{M_R}), and is the image of I^∨(φ^∨)(g) = ∫_{U_R} φ^∨(zg) dz (3.34). For GL_k, every τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) is the full induced representation ×_i |det|^{a_i} τ_i with τ_i tempered and a_1 > ⋯ > a_d.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): (3.16)–(3.17), Corollary 3.9 and all of §3.6 write π as a Langlands quotient, and §3.6 uses π ≅ Im(I) and π^∨ ≅ Im(I^∨). SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2–SR.3 and AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 plan induction, admissibility and globalisation, but not the classification for G_c. ET.6 plans segment and Langlands-quotient theory only for p-adic GL_m. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Archimedean Langlands parametrisation, with central and infinitesimal characters
items.statement: Let F be archimedean. Every π ∈ Irr(G) is parametrised by an admissible homomorphism φ_π: W_F → Ĝ, and Irr(GL_N) is in bijection with the admissible homomorphisms W_F → GL_N(C) [Lan89]. The representation T(π) with parameter r_G ∘ φ_π has central character χ_π^{N/2} ([Lan89]; [AS06, pp. 178–179] for GSpin_c). The infinitesimal character of π is determined by φ_π [NP21, Lemma 1].
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §3.2, p. 12, citing [Lan89] and [AS06, pp. 178–179]; §2, p. 9, footnote to Definition 2.2, citing [NP21, Lemma 1]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The archimedean transfer T(π), the archimedean L- and ε-factors of §3.4 and (3.13) are all defined through [Lan89], and its compatibility with central and infinitesimal characters is used for (3.1) and Definition 2.2. No item covers it, and no stage plans it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Theorem 3.12 for k = 1 (classical doubling)
items.statement: Let F be local, π ∈ Irr_rel,a.u.(G), and τ a unitary quasi-character of F^* (k = 1). For each s with Re(s) ≥ 1/2 there are a matrix coefficient ω of π^∨ and a K_H-finite f ∈ V(τ, c) such that Z(s, ω, f)/L(s, π × τ) is nonzero at s (possibly with a pole).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 3.12 for k = 1 is not proved in the paper. It 'already follows from the proof of [Yam14, Theorem 7.1], with minor adjustments for the groups (in ibid. the full orthogonal groups O_c were considered, and GSpin_c was not considered)'. The converse theorem needs k = 1 (twists by Hecke characters), and every §3.6 item assumes k > 1, so this input is missing. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Inductive realisation of the (k, c) functional
items.statement: Let τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k) be unitary, k > 1, and 0 < l < c. Then ρ_c(τ) is a subrepresentation of Ind_{R_(kl,k(c−l))}^{GL_kc}((W_ψ(ρ_l(τ)) ⊗ W_ψ(ρ_{c−l}(τ))) δ_{R_(kl,k(c−l))}^{−1/(2k)}). Let κ_{l,c−l} be the permutation matrix of Appendix A and V_l < U_(c^k) the abelian group generated by the blocks V^3_{i,j} (i < j). The integral ξ ↦ ∫_{V_l} ξ(κ_{l,c−l} v) dv converges absolutely and is a (k, c) functional on ρ_c(τ) [CFGK23, §3.2, Lemma 9]. Applied twice, with κ = diag(I_{kl}, κ_{c−2l,l}) κ_{l,c−l}, it realises the functional for the composition (l, c − 2l, l) used in Lemma 3.16.
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §3.6, pp. 21–22, proof of Lemma 3.16; Appendix A, p. 44, citing [CFGK23, §3.2, Lemma 9]; arXiv:1802.02637v5, Appendix A, p. 44, (A.4)-(A.5), citing [CFGK23, §3.2, Lemma 9]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 3.16 and Appendix A both rest on [CFGK23, §3.2, Lemma 9], and they use it only for unitary τ, which is the root of E1. No item covers it. (Both checkers proposed this; merged with 'Realization of the (k,c) functional of ρ_c(τ) through a composition of c'.) Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Matrix coefficients via intertwining integrals and the unfolding of Z along R
items.statement: Let π be the Langlands quotient of σ ⋊ π′ as in (3.16), ε = σ ⊗ π′, φ ∈ Ind_R^G(ε ∘ i_{M_R}) and φ^∨ ∈ Ind_{R^−}^G(ε^∨ ∘ i_{M_R}). Then ω_{φ,φ^∨}(g) = ∫_{M_R\G} ⟨φ(g_0), φ^∨(g_0 g)⟩ dg_0 = ∫_{R^−\G} ∫_{U_R^−} ⟨φ(yo), φ^∨(og)⟩ dy do converges absolutely and is a matrix coefficient of π^∨ (3.35). Substituting it into Z(s, ω_{φ,φ^∨}, f) and applying Lemma 3.3 twice gives the iterated integral (3.39), in Re(s) ≫ 0 and where absolutely convergent (justified by Lemma 3.20 for archimedean F and by the proof of Corollary 3.21 for non-archimedean F). Its inner integral is Z^1(s, ω^{e_G}_{φ,φ^∨}, f) = ∫_{U_R} ∫_{C°_G\M_R} ∫_{U_R^−} ∫_{U_0} δ_{R^−}^{−1/2}(m) ω^{e_G}_{φ,φ^∨}(m) f(s, δ u_0 e_2(^ι(zym))) ψ_U(u_0) du_0 dy dm dz (3.40), where ω^{e_G}_{φ,φ^∨}(m) = ⟨φ(e_G), ε^∨(m) φ^∨(e_G)⟩.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): This is the first step of the proof of Theorem 3.12. The formula for ω_{φ,φ^∨}, the identity Z = (3.39) and the definition of Z^1 are used by Propositions 3.18–3.19, Lemma 3.20 and Corollary 3.21. Z1-open-cell only names Z^1. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Bounds for smooth matrix coefficients of tempered representations
items.statement: Let F be archimedean, M a real reductive group (here M_R) and σ an irreducible tempered representation of M, with invariant inner product on its smooth space V_σ. There is a continuous seminorm β on V_σ with |⟨σ(m)v, w⟩| ≤ β(v) β(w) Ξ(m) for all v, w ∈ V_σ and m ∈ M, where Ξ is Harish-Chandra's basic spherical function [Sun09, Theorem 1.2]. If Re(ν) lies in the positive chamber for R, then ∫_{U_R^−} e^{⟨Re(ν) + ρ_R, H_{M_R}(m_u)⟩} Ξ(m_u) du < ∞, where u = r_u m_u k_u is the Iwasawa decomposition ([Wal88], proof of Lemma 5.3.1).
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §3.6, pp. 32–33, proof of Lemma 3.22, citing [Sun09, Theorem 1.2] and [Wal88, Lemma 5.3.1]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): These are the two inputs of Lemma 3.22, which is needed because §3.6 requires convergence of I against smooth, not only K-finite, vectors. No stage plans them. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Coarse transfers and supercuspidal support
items.statement: Let F be non-archimedean and π ∈ Irr(G). If Π ∈ Irr(GL_N) is a coarse transfer of π, then so is every Π′ ∈ Irr(GL_N) with the same supercuspidal support as Π [JPSS83, Theorem 3.1]. Conversely, the supercuspidal support of a coarse transfer, if one exists, depends only on π [Hen02, Proposition 1.9].
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §3.5, p. 18, citing [JPSS83, Theorem 3.1] and [Hen02, Proposition 1.9]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): These are stated results of §3.5, cited in the introduction (p. 2) as consequences of Theorem 4.10: for any weak transfer Π, the supercuspidal support of Π_ν is determined by π_ν. No item covers them. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Weak transfer of all irreducible automorphic representations
items.statement: Let F be a number field. Every irreducible automorphic representation π of G(A) has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N(A). By [Lan79b], π is a constituent of a representation parabolically induced from an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a Levi subgroup GL_{β_1} × ⋯ × GL_{β_d} × G_{c−2l}. Theorem 0.1 applies to the G_{c−2l} factor, and the transfer is the corresponding isobaric sum.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Stated as a consequence ('immediately extends'), with a one-line argument via [Lan79b]. It is a stated result of the paper that no item covers. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Twisted Euler products for the converse theorem: convergence and independence of ψ
items.statement: Let F be a number field, ψ a nontrivial character of F\A, Π = ⊗'Π_ν an irreducible admissible representation of GL_N(A), and τ a cuspidal representation of GL_k(A). Put L(s, Π × τ) = ∏_ν L(s, Π_ν × τ_ν) and ε(s, Π × τ, ψ) = ∏_ν ε(s, Π_ν × τ_ν, ψ_ν), with the Rankin–Selberg factors of [JPSS83, JS90] (for non-generic Π_ν, [JPSS83, §9.4]). (i) If ∏_ν L(s, Π_ν) converges absolutely in some right half-plane, so does L(s, Π × τ) ([CPS94, Lemma 2.2]). (ii) If the central character of Π is trivial on F^*, then ε(s, Π × τ, ψ), a finite product, is independent of ψ and is written ε(s, Π × τ) ([CPS94, Lemma 2.1]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 2.1 uses ε(s, Π × τ) without ψ, and §4.4 checks the absolute convergence of L(s, Π) only. Both steps rest on these two lemmas, and no item states them. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Holomorphy of the rank-one Siegel Eisenstein series away from twisted self-duality
items.statement: Let k >= 1, H_1 = G_2k (of the type of H), P its standard Siegel parabolic, τ a unitary cuspidal representation of GL_k(A), and θ a unitary Hecke character (θ = 1 unless H_1 = GSpin_2k). The constant term of E_{τ,θ,1}(h; s, f) along P is f(s, h) + M_0(s)f(s, h) (4.2), with M_0(s): |det|^s τ ⋊ θ → |det|^{-s}θτ^∨ ⋊ θ the standard intertwining operator. When H_1 = SO_2k or GSpin_2k with k odd, the constant terms along P and ^ȷP are f and M_0 f, and M_0 maps into the representation induced from ^ȷP, (4.8). If |det|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all t ∈ R, then M_0(s), and hence E_{τ,θ,1}(h; s, f), is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 0 ([MW95, Remark IV.3.12]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): This is the base case of the induction in Theorem 4.1, and it is also used for M_1 in Lemma 4.3 and for the holomorphy of b^S in Theorem 4.8. It is cited from [MW95] and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Constant term of E_{τ,θ,c} along the parabolic with Levi GL_k × G_{2k(c-1)}
items.statement: Let c >= 2, c' = c - 1, H' = G_{2kc'}, and let R, R' be the standard maximal parabolics of H = G_2kc with M_R ≅ GL_k × H' and M_{R'} ≅ GL_{kc'} × G_2k. For an entire section f as in (4.1), the constant term f_{P_{(k,kc')}} lies in |det|^{s-c'/2}τ ⋊ (|det|^{s+1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) ⋊ θ), and f_{P_{(kc',k)}} lies in |det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) ⋊ (|det|^{s+c'/2}τ ⋊ θ) (4.3). Let M_1, M_2 be as in Lemma 4.3 and M_1^□, M_2^□ the induced operators, so that M_2^□(s)M_1^□(s) maps into |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ ⋊ (|det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) ⋊ θ) (4.4). Then (E_{τ,θ,c})_R(s, f) = E_{τ,θ,c'}(s + 1/2, f_{P_{(k,kc')}}) + E_{τ,θ,c'}(s - 1/2, M_2^□(s)M_1^□(s) f_{P_{(kc',k)}}) (4.5) ([JLZ13, Proposition 2.3]). For H = SO_2kc or GSpin_2kc with k odd and k > 1, the second term is E^ȷ_{τ,θ,c'}(s - 1/2, ^ȷM_2^□M_1^□ f_{P_{(kc',k)}}), with M_0 as in (4.8) and E^ȷ the series for ^ȷP (4.9); a similar formula holds for E^ȷ_{τ,θ,c}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The inductive constant-term formula drives both Lemma 4.4 and the proof of Theorem 4.1. It is cited from [JLZ13] and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Eisenstein series: regularity on the unitary axis and detection of poles by cuspidal constant terms
items.statement: Let τ be unitary cuspidal on GL_k(A), θ unitary, and E = E_{τ,θ,c} as in (4.1). (i) E(h; s, f) is holomorphic on Re(s) = 0 ([MW95, Theorem VI.2.1(i)]). (ii) M_{P_{(k^c)}} is the only standard Levi subgroup of H contributing to the cuspidal support of E; so is ^ȷM_{P_{(k^c)}} when H = SO_2kc or GSpin_2kc with k odd and k > 1. Hence a pole s_0 of E is a pole of its constant term along P_{(k^c)} (or ^ȷP_{(k^c)}), and so of its constant term along R ([MW95, Lemma I.4.10]).
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.2, proof of Theorem 4.1, pp. 36-37, citing [MW95, Theorem VI.2.1(i), Lemma I.4.10]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Theorem 4.1 opens with these two cited facts, and no item covers them. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Square-integrability criterion and Hermitian symmetry of residual cuspidal data
items.statement: Let H = G_2kc and M = M_{P_{(k^c)}}. (i) ([MW95, §I.4.11]) Let an automorphic form on H(A) have cuspidal support along P_{(k^c)} (and ^ȷP_{(k^c)} when it also contributes). Suppose the real parts of all its cuspidal exponents lie in the open negative cone; with M ≅ GL_k^c this reads Σ_{i<=j} Re(e_i) < 0 for 1 <= j <= c. Then the form is square-integrable. (ii) ([MW95, Theorem V.3.13(iii), V.3.14, Corollary V.3.16, Remark V.3.6(b)]) Let a nonzero square-integrable automorphic form on H(A) have cuspidal support in the W(M)-orbit 𝔆 of a cuspidal datum Ξ. Then it lies in L²(H(F)\H(A))_𝔆 ≠ 0, and the Hermitian dual Ξ* (the complex conjugate of the contragredient) lies in 𝔆, i.e. Ξ* = wΞ for some w ∈ W(M).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The key contradiction in Theorem 4.1 comes from these facts: the leading coefficient is square-integrable, so its cuspidal datum is Hermitian-self-dual up to W. No item covers them. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Normalization of the intertwining operator between a Speh and a cuspidal representation of GL
items.statement: Let τ be unitary cuspidal on GL_k(A), θ a unitary Hecke character, and c' >= 1. The standard intertwining operator M_2(s): |det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) × |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ → |det|^{-s-c'/2}θτ^∨ × |det|^{s-1/2}ρ_{c'}(τ) on GL_kc(A) satisfies the following: [L(2s + c', τ × θ^{-1}τ)/L(2s, τ × θ^{-1}τ)] M_2(s) is holomorphic in Re(s - 1/2) > Re(-s - c'/2), i.e. in Re(s) > (1 - c')/4 ([MW89, §I.10]). Equivalently, M_2(s) = [L(2s, τ × θ^{-1}τ)/L(2s + c', τ × θ^{-1}τ)] N_2(s) with N_2 holomorphic there.
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 36, citing [MW89, §I.10]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The holomorphy of M_2 rests on this normalization, and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Poles and non-vanishing of global Rankin–Selberg L-functions
items.statement: Let τ and τ' be unitary cuspidal representations of GL_k(A) and GL_{k'}(A), and S a finite set of places. L^S(s, τ × τ') and L(s, τ × τ') converge absolutely, and are holomorphic and nonvanishing, in Re(s) > 1. They are nonvanishing on Re(s) = 1, and holomorphic there except for a simple pole at s = 1 - iy when τ' ≅ τ^∨|det|^{iy} ([JS81a, JS81b, Sha81]). In particular, if θ is unitary and |det|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ for all t ∈ R, then L(s, τ × θ^{-1}τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1. For c >= 2, L^S(s + c/2, τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2 ([JS81b]).
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 36, and §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.8, p. 39
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.8 use these global facts about GL Rankin–Selberg L-functions, and no item states them. Status: AL.3 plans the global unfolding for cuspidal data and 'analytic nonvanishing results only in their proved regions'.

items.name: Global generalized Speh representation ρ_c(τ)
items.statement: Let τ be a unitary cuspidal representation of GL_k(A) and c >= 1. The generalized Speh representation ρ_c(τ) of GL_kc(A) ([Jac84, §2.4]; [MW89]) is the irreducible automorphic representation spanned by the iterated residues, at λ = ((c-1)/2, (c-3)/2, ..., (1-c)/2), of the Eisenstein series induced from |det|^{λ_1}τ ⊗ ... ⊗ |det|^{λ_c}τ on R_{(k^c)}. It lies in the discrete spectrum, and ρ_c(τ) ≅ ⊗'_ν ρ_c(τ_ν) with the local ρ_c(τ_ν) of §3.1. The unfolding of [GK23, §3.2] behind (4.10) uses its Fourier coefficient along (U_{(c^k)}, ψ_k), which factors through the local (k,c) models W_ψ(ρ_c(τ_ν)) (as used in §4.3). For a Hecke character χ, ρ_c(χτ) = χ(det)ρ_c(τ); §4.3 uses this with χ = χ_π.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The definition behind (4.1), and hence behind every item in §4, is this global residual representation. Item speh covers only the local ρ_c(τ_ν). Status: ET.7a plans 'the required GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification … from the Arthur–Clozel and Moeglin–Waldspurger proofs', of which the residual representation ρ_c(τ) of GL_kc is part.

items.name: Holomorphy of the normalizing factor b^S(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π)
items.statement: Let c >= 2, and let π and τ be unitary cuspidal representations of G(A) and GL_k(A) with |det|^{it}χ_πτ ≇ τ^∨ for all t ∈ R. Let S be a finite set of places containing S_∞, outside which π, τ and ψ are unramified. Then L^S(s, τ, ∧² ⊗ χ_π) and L^S(s, τ, ∨² ⊗ χ_π) are holomorphic in Re(s) >= 0 ([MW95, Remark IV.3.12] and a standard argument, see [Kim00, (1.3)]). L^S(s + c/2, τ), a factor of b^S only when G = Sp_c, is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2 ([JS81b]). Hence b^S(s, c, τ ⊗ χ_π) of (3.3) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2. Under the same hypothesis b^S is even entire ([KS02, Proposition 2.1]).
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.8, p. 39 and footnote 3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): The left side of (4.11) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2 only if b^S is. The paper proves this inside the proof of Theorem 4.8, and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Highly ramified twists are not twisted-self-dual
items.statement: Let π be a unitary cuspidal representation of G(A), S a nonempty finite set of finite places, and η a unitary Hecke character of A^* with η_{ν_0}² χ_{π_{ν_0}} nontrivial on O^*_{ν_0} for some ν_0 ∈ S. Then for every τ ∈ A(S, η) (§2) and every t ∈ R, |det|^{it}χ_πτ ≇ τ^∨ (see the proof of [CKPSS01, Lemma 3.2]). The proof of Theorem 0.1 also uses that such η exist and can be taken arbitrarily highly ramified at every ν ∈ S.
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.4, proof of Theorem 0.1, pp. 40-41, citing the proof of [CKPSS01, Lemma 3.2]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): This is how the proof of Theorem 0.1 verifies hypothesis (1) of Theorem 4.8 for every τ ∈ A(S_π, η). No item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Globalization of supercuspidal representations
items.statement: (i) Let F be a number field, ν_0 a finite place, and σ' a supercuspidal representation of GL_l(F_{ν_0}). There is a cuspidal representation σ of GL_l(A) with σ_{ν_0} ≅ σ' and σ_ν unramified at every finite ν ≠ ν_0 ([Hen84, Appendice 1]). (ii) Let f be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0, G = G_c split, and π' a supercuspidal representation of G(f). There are a number field F with a place ν such that F_ν ≅ f, and a cuspidal representation π of G(A) with π_ν ≅ π'. The paper cites this as 'see e.g., [Hen84, Appendice 1]', whose Poincaré-series argument is written for GL_n.
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.10, p. 41, and of Corollary 4.11, p. 42, citing [Hen84, Appendice 1]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 4.10 and Corollary 4.11 both globalize a supercuspidal representation, and no item covers it. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika classification: automorphic representations of GL_N agreeing almost everywhere
items.statement: Every irreducible automorphic representation Π of GL_N(A) is a constituent of Ind(σ_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ σ_r) for cuspidal, not necessarily unitary, σ_i of GL_{n_i}(A) with Σ n_i = N ([Lan79b]). If Π and Π' are irreducible automorphic representations of GL_N(A) with Π_ν ≅ Π'_ν for almost all ν, their cuspidal data {σ_i} coincide up to permutation ([JS81a, Theorem 4.4]). So at every place ν, Π_ν and Π'_ν are constituents of the same induced representation, and γ^RS(s, Π_ν × τ, ψ_ν) = γ^RS(s, Π'_ν × τ, ψ_ν) for every τ ∈ Irr(GL_k(F_ν)) (multiplicativity, [JPSS83, JS90]).

items.name: Crude functional equation for partial Rankin–Selberg L-functions
items.statement: Let Π be an irreducible automorphic representation of GL_N(A), σ a cuspidal representation of GL_l(A), and ψ a nontrivial character of F\A. Let S be a finite set of places containing S_∞, outside which Π, σ and ψ are unramified. Then L^S(s, Π × σ) = ∏_{ν∈S} γ^RS(s, Π_ν × σ_ν, ψ_ν) L^S(1 - s, Π^∨ × σ^∨) as meromorphic functions ([Cog04, CPS04]).
