items.name: Equivariance of (k,c) functions under the diagonal GL_c
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, c, k >= 1, and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). For every W ∈ W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)) and g ∈ GL_c, W(e_1(g)e_2(g)) = W(diag(g, ..., g)) = τ(det g) W(I_kc), with g repeated k times and τ(a) the central character of τ at aI_k ([CFGK23, Lemma 12]).

items.name: Analytic properties of the GL_c × GL_k integrals
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0, c >= 1, k > 1, π ∈ Irr(GL_c), and τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k). Z(s, ω, W, φ), and Z for k > 1, converges absolutely in Re(s) >> 0 independently of the data (Lemma 3.13 and a bound on matrix coefficients). For each s it can be made holomorphic and nonzero near s; over a non-archimedean field it can be made identically 1. Z* has the same properties in a left half-plane. Its dz-integration contributes no poles: it can be removed by [DM78] and conjugation. Over a non-archimedean field, Z and Z* are rational in q^{-s} for all π and generic τ, by Theorem A.1, the constant choice, and Bernstein's continuation principle ([Ban98]). If moreover τ is unitary and π is unramified or F is archimedean, Z and Z* continue meromorphically to C, continuously in (ω, W) over archimedean fields. The proof reduces through (A.7), (A.8), (A.14) and (A.17) to Rankin–Selberg integrals for GL_1 × GL_k ([JPSS83, JS90, Jac09]; [Sou95, §5, Lemmas 1-2]).

items.name: ε-factor and functional equation of the GL_c × GL_k integrals
items.statement: Under the standing assumptions of Theorem A.6, there is ε(s, π × τ, ψ) ∈ F^* such that for all ω and W, ε(s, π × τ, ψ) Z(s, ω, W)/fraktur-L(s, π × τ) = π(-1)^{k-1} Z*(s, ω, W)/fraktur-L(1 - s, π^∨ × τ^∨) (A.18). Together with (A.3) this gives γ(s, π × τ, ψ) = ε(s, π × τ, ψ) fraktur-L(1 - s, π^∨ × τ^∨)/fraktur-L(s, π × τ) (A.19).

items.name: Exponents of unitary generic representations of GL_k
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0. Every unitary τ ∈ Irr_gen(GL_k(F)) is irreducibly induced as τ ≅ |det|^{α_1}δ_1 × ... × |det|^{α_r}δ_r, with δ_i square-integrable and α_i real, |α_i| < 1/2. Consequently, for tempered σ_0 ∈ Irr(GL_l(F)), L^RS(s, σ_0 × τ) is holomorphic in Re(s) >= 1/2. So for a ∈ R the poles of L(s + a, σ_0 × τ) lie in Re(s) + a < 1/2, and those of L(1 - s - a, σ_0^∨ × τ^∨) lie in Re(s) + a > 1/2.

items.name: Dixmier–Malliavin factorization
items.statement: Let V be a smooth Fréchet representation of moderate growth of a real Lie group Γ, for instance a unipotent group Mat_{a×b}(R) or Mat_{a×b}(C) acting on ρ_c(τ) or on W_ψ(ρ_c(τ)). Every v ∈ V is a finite sum Σ_i π(φ_i)v_i with φ_i ∈ C_c^∞(Γ) and v_i ∈ V ([DM78]). Over non-archimedean fields the analogue is immediate: v = vol(K)^{-1}π(1_K)v for any open compact K fixing v.

(Both checkers proposed this; merged with 'Dixmier–Malliavin factorisation'.) Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling.

items.name: Langlands classification for GL_c
items.statement: Let F be local of characteristic 0. Every π ∈ Irr(GL_c(F)) is the unique irreducible quotient of a standard module Ind_{R_β}^{GL_c}(|det|^{a_1}σ_{1,0} ⊗ ... ⊗ |det|^{a_d}σ_{d,0}), with σ_{i,0} ∈ Irr(GL_{β_i}) tempered and real a_1 > ... > a_d; the data are unique up to isomorphism. π is the image of the absolutely convergent intertwining operator Ind_R^{GL_c}(σ_1 ⊗ π') → Ind_{R^-}^{GL_c}(σ_1 ⊗ π'), where R = R_{(β_1,c-β_1)} and π' is the Langlands quotient of the remaining data. π^∨ is the unique irreducible quotient of the standard module with data (|det|^{-a_d}σ_{d,0}^∨, ..., |det|^{-a_1}σ_{1,0}^∨). If F is non-archimedean and π is unramified, every σ_{i,0} is unramified.
items.locator: arXiv:1802.02637v5, Appendix A, Lemma A.8 and Proposition A.10, pp. 51-54
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 (coverage of the paper): Lemma A.8 and Proposition A.10 are stated and proved through Langlands data. Nothing in the atlas plans the Langlands classification; the route brief assumes SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups has it, but SR.0-SR.6 do not. routes.title: Automorphic L-functions and local factors, Part II: the generalized doubling method and functorial transfer for classical groups
routes.brief:
Automorphic L-functions and local factors, extended to the generalized doubling method of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg, Gourevitch and Kaplan for split symplectic, special orthogonal and general spin groups twisted by GL_k. Cover generalized Speh representations and their (k, c) models; the local doubling integrals with their γ-, L- and ε-factors (characterization, compatibility with the unramified and archimedean transfer, stability, holomorphy for tempered data) and the attainment of the poles in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 through the GL_c × GL_k integrals of Kaplan's appendix; the doubling Eisenstein series and its holomorphy away from twisted self-duality; the global integral, functional equation and entireness of twisted L-functions; and the Cogdell–Kim–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shahidi converse theorem. Final theorems: every cuspidal representation of such a group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), weak transfers are coarse transfers at every place (Theorem 4.10), and local coarse transfers exist (Corollary 4.11). Import Rankin–Selberg factors from layer AL.3, the Satake isomorphism from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (SR.4), and parabolic induction and Langlands quotients from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.

This is the same Part II id as route 1 of PAPER-EISCHEN-HARRIS-LI-ETAL-20, which proposes it under the title 'Part II: the doubling method for classical and unitary groups' and adds the classical doubling method for unitary groups; the design job should adopt one title covering both briefs. PAPER-ATOBE-KONDO-YASUDA-22 proposes a separate Part II, AutomorphicLFunctionsPartIISpehIntegrals, for Speh-model integrals on GL_n; the (k, c) models here should be designed compatibly with it.

Also import: the GL_m residual spectrum and Speh classification from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a (for the global ρ_c(τ)), and global Rankin–Selberg poles and non-vanishing from AL.3. The GL_N converse theorem of Cogdell–Piatetski-Shapiro (with the η-twists of CKPSS), the Langlands classification for G_c and GL_c, Dixmier–Malliavin, the Mœglin–Waldspurger Eisenstein-series inputs and the Jacquet–Shalika classification are planned nowhere and are built here.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24):
- Propositions 3.17 and 3.19 and Corollary 3.21 must be stated for unitary χ_π, or reduced to that case by the twist χ_π = |·|^r χ_0 (E1). Theorem 3.12 needs only the unitary case.
- In (3.16) the Langlands data satisfy a_d > r, not r/2.
- The coarse-transfer definition (3.18) should quantify over generic τ, the only ones for which the doubling γ-factor is defined.
- Lemma 4.3's holomorphy of M_2(s) in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 needs L(2s, τ × θ^{−1}τ) holomorphic and L(2s + c′, τ × θ^{−1}τ) non-vanishing there; the printed proof swaps the two. The first uses the non-self-duality hypothesis of Theorem 4.1, so state Lemma 4.3 under it.
- In the proof of Theorem 4.10, check that the central character of Π_ν is χ_{π_ν}^{N/2} before applying Theorem 3.10.
- Proposition A.10 says that L^RS(s, π × τ)/𝔏(s, π × τ) is entire, where 𝔏 is the gcd of Theorem A.6. The extraction had this reversed.
routes.reason: The doubling integrals, their local factors, the Eisenstein-series analysis and the converse-theorem transfer extend the atlas's automorphic L-function roadmap; its Rankin–Selberg layer AL.3 and the Satake layer SR.4 are imported rather than re-planned.

sourceIssues.printed: 'the operator L(2s+c′,τ×θ^{−1}τ)/L(2s,τ×θ^{−1}τ) M_2(s) is holomorphic when Re(s−1/2) > Re(−s−c′/2) ... By [JS81a, JS81b, Sha81], L(2s+c′,τ×θ^{−1}τ) is holomorphic when Re(2s+c′) > 1, hence in Re(s) > 0, and L(2s,τ×θ^{−1}τ) is nonvanishing when Re(2s) ≥ 1, i.e., in Re(s) ≥ 1/2. Therefore M_2(s) is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 1/2.'
sourceIssues.correction: Since [L(2s+c′)/L(2s)]·M_2(s) = N_2(s) is holomorphic, M_2(s) = [L(2s, τ×θ^{−1}τ)/L(2s+c′, τ×θ^{−1}τ)]·N_2(s). Holomorphy in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 therefore needs two facts. First, L(2s+c′, τ×θ^{−1}τ) is nonvanishing there, which holds because Re(2s+c′) ≥ 1+c′ ≥ 2. Second, L(2s, τ×θ^{−1}τ) is holomorphic there. It converges absolutely for Re(2s) > 1. On Re(2s) = 1 it could only have a pole at 2s = 1 − it with θ^{−1}τ ≅ τ^∨|det|^{it}, i.e. |det|^{−it}τ ≅ θτ^∨ ([JS81a, JS81b]), which the hypothesis of Theorem 4.1 excludes. So Lemma 4.3 remains true, but the M_2 part uses the hypothesis |det|^{it}τ ≇ θτ^∨ as well.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed argument gives holomorphy to the wrong L-function and nonvanishing to the wrong one. Poles of M_2 can come only from poles of L(2s) or zeros of L(2s+c′), so holomorphy of L(2s+c′) and nonvanishing of L(2s) say nothing about M_2. The displayed normalization is itself right: the Gindikin–Karpelevich factors L(x_j − y)/L(1 + x_j − y), with x_j − y = 2s + c′ − 1 − j for j = 0, ..., c′−1, telescope to L(2s)/L(2s+c′). Check with k = c′ = 1 and τ = χ: M_2(s) acts on the spherical vector by L(2s, χ²)/L(2s+1, χ²). This is holomorphic in Re(s) ≥ 1/2 exactly when L(2s, χ²) has no pole on Re(2s) = 1, i.e. when χ² ≠ |·|^{it}, which is the hypothesis.

summaryBefore: Cai, Friedberg and Kaplan prove that every irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of a symplectic or quasi-split orthogonal group has a weak functorial transfer to GL_N (Theorem 0.1), without assuming genericity. They use the converse theorem, with twisted L-functions controlled by the generalized doubling method (local γ-factors, their stability, and a global analysis of the doubling Eisenstein series). They deduce that the transfer is a coarse transfer at every place, and that local coarse transfers exist. Partial first extraction (cc-442dc5): the main theorems and definitions are items; the remaining lemmas and propositions of §3 and §4 are listed in the handoff.
